newsitem.title: USA: Motorola feud could delay Iridium - report.
newsitem.headline: Motorola feud could delay Iridium - report.

text.p: A dispute between Motorola Inc and its Iridium unit could delay the satellite company's $186 million initial public offering, Business Week reported.
The companies are arguing over when Iridium will be up and running, allowing people to make voice calls and use pagers anywhere on earth, the weekly business news magazine said in its current issue.

Motorola said in financial documents that there is a delay in the launch of the satellite service because of problems with McDonnell Douglas Corp's rocket used to launch the satellites, the magazine said.

A Delta II rocket that is expected to launch the system blew up on January 17, leading to an investigation, it said. But Iridium claims there is no excuse for the delay because Motorola had missed four scheduled launch dates before the explosion.
Motorola was not immediately available for comment.
Delays could cost the company in the market place in an industry expected to reach $15 billion by 2005, it said.
"Our plan continues to be to launch the entire system on schedule," a Motorola spokesman told the magazine.
